newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica orders Placer Dome to clean up.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica orders Placer Dome to clean up.

text.p: The Costa Rican governnment ordered Canadian mining company Placer Dome to partially suspend exploration for gold in the north of the country on charges of environmental damage, a government spokesman said on Friday.
"The government gave the company notice of the order today and it is to be applied forthwith," Rene Castro, Minister of the Environment and Mining, told a news conference.
"The company's exploration and mining activities have eliminated parts of woodland and moved quantities of earth that have accumulated without adequate control," Castro said.

Castro said Placer Dome, headquartered in Vancouver, BC, had significantly harmed the the countryside and caused substantial damage to the ground, flora and fauna. Among the complaints was that Placer's drilling at the site was creating noise that disturbed local wildlife.
In Vancouver, Placer spokesman Hugh Leggatt said the company had caused no environmental damage at Cerro Crucitas, the site in question, and said he was surprised by the government order.
"This came without warning. ... We see no reason for it," he said.

The government granted Placer Dome three months to undertake necessary corrective measures to reduce and offset environmental damage caused, and obliged the firm to change working practices in order not to repeat the damage.
Placer Dome began operations in Costa Rica, near the border with Nicaragua, in 1993 on about 2,000 hectares (5,000 acres) granted in a government concession.
The government order to stop exploration was considered partial because it is applies to a 100-hectare (250-acre) area where Placer's activities are concentrated.

Placer said it believes it is still in compliance with an environmental impact statement previously agreed with the government. Leggatt said the suspension order appeared to stem from "subjective interpretations" of that environmental plan by the government.

The Cerro Crucitas project is undergoing prefeasibility work to determine if a mine would be economically viable. Placer has so far identified a resource of 2.2 million ounces of gold and invested US$20 million there, the spokesman said.
